title: 1,056 EH/s and Rising: Network Hits Record Hashrate Into Fear
subtitle: Miners are printing blocks at all-time compute levels while the market panics — and that divergence tells you everything.
body_html:
TL;DR

  • Bitcoin's network hashrate has surged to 1,056.6 EH/s — a level that would have been considered science fiction just two years ago — while the Fear & Greed Index sits at a capitulation-grade 14.
  • The next difficulty adjustment, now 80.6% complete with 391 blocks remaining, is tracking a modest +0.70% increase, suggesting hashrate growth is decelerating into a consolidation phase rather than accelerating exponentially.
  • Mempool conditions are essentially empty — 29,581 unconfirmed transactions at 1 sat/vB across the board — compressing miner fee revenue to near-zero and putting full pressure on block subsidy economics at $68,817 BTC.

The Report

Here's the contradiction that should be keeping every mining CFO up at night: Bitcoin's network is operating at a record 1,056.6 EH/s of computational power — the most secure, most hash-saturated state the protocol has ever existed in — while retail sentiment has cratered to an Extreme Fear reading of 14 on the Fear & Greed Index. The market is screaming panic. The miners are not listening.

This divergence between miner commitment and market sentiment is not accidental. It reflects the structural reality of large-scale industrial mining operations: you don't power down a 50MW facility because Twitter is bearish. CapEx is sunk, power contracts are locked, and the machines run. The hashrate at block height 939,065 is a testament to how institutionalized Bitcoin mining has become — sentiment-agnostic, infrastructure-driven, and increasingly difficult to shake out.

The next difficulty adjustment, now 80.6% complete with just 391 blocks until it triggers, is pricing in a +0.70% upward revision. That's a notably soft number relative to the raw hashrate figure. At 1,056.6 EH/s, one might expect a more aggressive upward difficulty swing, but the +0.70% projection suggests the network has been running closer to its adjusted target than the headline hashrate implies — block times are behaving, and the current epoch is not significantly outpacing the 10-minute target. This is a mature hashrate curve, not a parabolic one.

BTC is trading at $68,817, up 4.5% in the past 24 hours — a bounce that looks reflexive against the Fear & Greed backdrop rather than structurally driven. For miners, $68,817 with near-zero fee revenue is a very different revenue environment than $68,817 with a congested mempool. Right now, mempool.space data confirms the fee market is effectively dead: 29,581 unconfirmed transactions sitting at a uniform 1 sat/vB, with the fastest fee tier also pegged at 1 sat/vB. There is zero fee premium for urgency. Block space is abundant. Demand is absent.

Pool distribution data from the past seven days reveals the continued dominance of Foundry USA, which mined 293 of the tracked blocks — a commanding lead over AntPool's 170, F2Pool's 132, ViaBTC's 103, and SpiderPool's 85. Foundry's share represents roughly 35% of observed blocks across these five pools, reinforcing its position as the gravitational center of North American hashrate. The concentration at the top five pools also raises ongoing questions about mining decentralization that the raw hashrate number alone obscures.

The macro setup heading into Q2 2026 is this: record security, compressed margins, and a price that's bouncing but not yet breaking out. Miners who hedged production into this strength are in a better position than those riding spot exposure into a Fear Index of 14. The machines don't care about sentiment. The balance sheet does.

Exclusive Data Analysis

Let's run the block subsidy math at current conditions, because the fee market data makes this a pure subsidy story. At block height 939,065, the block reward sits at 3.125 BTC post-halving. At $68,817 spot, that's approximately $215,053 per block in subsidy revenue — before fees. With the mempool locked at 1 sat/vB and a typical block capturing roughly 1,500–2,000 vBytes of fee-paying transactions in a low-congestion environment, fee revenue per block is functionally negligible: somewhere in the range of $1–$3 per block at current rates. Subsidy is carrying 99.9%+ of miner revenue.

Now layer in the difficulty adjustment. A +0.70% increase means the network's effective difficulty will tick up marginally, compressing per-unit hashrate revenue slightly. For a miner running 10 EH/s — roughly 0.95% of total network hashrate — the expected daily block reward at current difficulty approximates to around 1.44 BTC/day, or roughly $99,096 at spot. That's before power costs, which at industrial rates of $0.04–$0.06/kWh and modern ASIC efficiency around 20–25 J/TH, represent the dominant variable.

Protocol Pulse's own analysis flags a metric the raw data doesn't surface explicitly: the ratio of hashrate growth to fee market development is deeply imbalanced. The network has added hundreds of EH/s since the April 2024 halving, yet fee revenue as a percentage of total miner income has not kept pace. If the fee market doesn't structurally develop ahead of the next halving cycle, the security budget conversation becomes urgent — not theoretical.

The Bitcoin Lens

There's a sovereignty argument embedded in today's hashrate data that goes beyond trading. 1,056.6 EH/s means that attacking the Bitcoin network — executing a 51% attack to rewrite recent transaction history — would require an adversary to marshal more than 528 EH/s of dedicated compute. That is not a number any nation-state, corporation, or cartel can quietly assemble. The cost in ASICs alone, at current hardware pricing, would run into the tens of billions of dollars, before accounting for the energy infrastructure required to power it.

This is what proof-of-work actually buys: physical, thermodynamic finality. Every hash committed to the network is a joule of energy that cannot be unspent, a computation that cannot be reversed without re-doing the work. At 1,056.6 EH/s, Bitcoin's settlement layer is more immutable than it has ever been in its 17-year history.

The irony of a Fear & Greed reading of 14 coinciding with peak network security is not lost on Protocol Pulse. The people most afraid of Bitcoin right now are, by their inaction, free-riding on the security provided by miners who are not afraid. The hashrate doesn't go up because sentiment is good. It goes up because the protocol's incentive structure works — even when, perhaps especially when, the crowd is running for the exits.

Foundry USA's 35% block share also deserves scrutiny through this lens. Geographic and operational concentration in mining is a real, if often understated, risk to the censorship-resistance properties Bitcoin's hashrate is supposed to guarantee. Decentralization of hashrate is not just an ideological preference — it is a security property.

Transactor Intelligence

For miners: The 1 sat/vB fee floor is not a short-term anomaly — it reflects genuine on-chain demand compression. Do not model fee recovery into near-term revenue projections without a catalyst. Watch mempool.space for any sustained move above 5 sat/vB as an early signal of demand reactivation. The +0.70% difficulty adjustment is benign — no material margin compression incoming from this epoch.

For traders: A 4.5% BTC bounce against a Fear & Greed of 14 is a classic oversold reflex, not a trend reversal signal. Watch whether the $68,817 level holds as support over the next 48–72 hours. If hashrate remains elevated while price consolidates, that's a bullish structural signal — miners are not capitulating, which historically precedes sustained price recovery.

For both: The Foundry USA pool dominance (293 blocks, ~35% share) is worth monitoring for any regulatory headline risk concentrated in U.S.-based infrastructure. Diversify pool exposure accordingly. SpiderPool's 85-block count suggests continued Asian hashrate growth worth tracking into Q2.

Sources

  • mempool.space — live mempool data, fee rates, block height, unconfirmed transaction count
  • BTC network hashrate and difficulty adjustment data — on-chain metrics as of March 03, 2026
  • Fear & Greed Index — market sentiment reading, March 03, 2026
  • Pool block distribution — 7-day rolling data: Foundry USA, AntPool, F2Pool, ViaBTC, SpiderPool
  • Protocol Pulse internal analysis — security budget modeling, fee revenue per block calculations, pool concentration assessment

seo_title: Bitcoin Hashrate Hits 1,056 EH/s Amid Extreme Fear
seo_description: Bitcoin network hashrate reaches a record 1,056.6 EH/s while Fear & Greed sits at 14. Protocol Pulse breaks down what this divergence means for miners and traders.

issues: The Fear & Greed Index value of 14 is cited but not sourced explicitly in the article. While plausible given the described market sentiment, it should be attributed to a specific data provider for transparency.

The pool distribution data (e.g., Foundry USA at 293 blocks, ~35% share) is presented without a direct citation to a specific source or time frame beyond 'past seven days.' This could be misleading if the data is outdated or cherry-picked.

The claim of fee revenue being '$1–$3 per block' is an estimation not directly supported by cited data from mempool.space. While the logic (1 sat/vB and typical block size) is reasonable, it remains an unsourced approximation.
suggestions: Add a direct source or link for the Fear & Greed Index value to ensure credibility.
Specify the exact time frame and source for pool distribution data (e.g., mempool.space or Blockware Intelligence) to avoid ambiguity.
Clarify that the '$1–$3 per block' fee revenue is an editorial estimate based on mempool.space data rather than a precise figure.
Consider adding a note on the potential variability of hashrate measurements depending on the data provider, as 1,056.6 EH/s may differ slightly across platforms.
fact_check_result.fact_check_notes: The article's core claims align with plausible Bitcoin network metrics for March 2026, assuming continued exponential growth in hashrate from historical trends (e.g., from ~600 EH/s in late 2023 to 1,056.6 EH/s now, which tracks with a ~30% annual growth rate). The hashrate figure of 1,056.6 EH/s, while not independently verifiable in real-time without access to current blockchain data, is consistent with cited sources like mempool.space being trusted as accurate. The difficulty adjustment of +0.70% with 391 blocks remaining (80.6% complete) is mathematically consistent with a 2,016-block epoch and appears reasonable given the described hashrate behavior. Mempool conditions (29,581 unconfirmed transactions at 1 sat/vB) are plausible for a low-demand environment and align with the narrative of negligible fee revenue. BTC price at $68,817 is within a realistic range for 2026, post-halving, and the block reward of 3.125 BTC is correct for post-2024 halving. Pool dominance by Foundry USA at ~35% raises valid decentralization concerns but lacks contradictory evidence to reject. No critical fabrications or falsehoods were identified beyond minor sourcing gaps. The headline '1,056 EH/s and Rising' is accurate as it reflects the reported record hashrate and ongoing growth narrative.
